en: I had no hope of success, O Sanjaya, when I heard that having been requested, Arjuna, piercing the ground, had allayed the thirst of Bhishma when he very much longed for water.

sa: एष मे दक्षिणो राजन् पाणिस्ताननखाङ्गुलिः॥ समुद्धर गृहीत्वा मां कुलीनस्त्वं हि मे मतः। जानामि त्वां हि संशान्तं वीर्यवन्तं यशस्विनम्॥ तस्मान्मां पतितामस्मात् कूपादुद्धर्तुमर्हसि।
en: O king, this is my right hand with nails as bright as the burnished copper. You are nobly born, I ask you, take my hand and raise me up. I know, you are very gentle, very powerful and greatly famous. You should raise me up from this well.

sa: निवृत्तिश्चागता सौम्य संतापश्च निराकृतः। भवद्वाक्यैः सुरुचिरैरनुनीतोऽस्मि लक्ष्मण॥
en: O gentle Saumitrī, my grief and sorrow have been removed for those pleasant words of yours.

sa: दह्यन्त्यङ्गानि मे भद्रे न दिशः प्रतिभान्ति च। सीदामीव च संमोहात् घूर्णतीव च मे मनः॥
en: “O amiable sister, my body is burning. I can no longer see the points of the heavens. I am about to fall owing to the loss of consciousness. My mind is whirling.

sa: अमषिते सुसंरब्धे दास्ये कृतपणे तदा। जग्मतुस्तुरगं द्रष्टुमुच्चैःश्रवसमन्तिकात्॥
en: Having laid an wager of slavery and burning with jealously, went to see the horse Uchchaishrava.

sa: तस्यैवं भाषमाणस्य हसतश्च मुहुर्मुहुः। शत्रुघ्नो वीर्यसंपन्नो रोषादश्रूण्यासृजत्॥
en: Lavaņa having said this again and again laughing the great hero Satrughna shed tears in anger.

sa: महासेनश्च राजेन्द्र सदोपास्ते पितामहम्। देवो नारायणस्तस्यां तथा देवर्षयश्च ये॥ ऋषयो बालखिल्याश्च योनिजायोनिचास्तथा। यच्च किंचित् त्रिलोकेऽस्मिन् दृश्यते स्थाणु जङ्गमम्। सर्वं तस्यां मया दृष्टमिति विद्धि नराधिप।॥
en: O king of kings, Mahasena also worship the Grandsire, know, O king, that Narayana himself, the celestials Rishis, the Rishis named Balkhilyas, all beings born of females or not born of females, nay whatever else is seen in the three worlds, mobile and immobile, were all seen by me there in that assembly-hall (of Brahma).

sa: निवेदयन्ति स्म तदा कुन्त्या भैक्षं सदा निशि। तया विभक्तान् भागांस्ते भुञ्जते स्म पृथक् पृथक्॥
en: They offered to Kunti every night all the food (that they got during the day) and it (the food) was divided (by Kunti) and they each ate separately the share of each.

sa: गुरुणा चाननुज्ञातो ग्राहयेद् यत् सुतो मम। न स कुर्यात् तथा कार्यं विद्ययेति सतां मतम्॥
en: The opinion of the learned men is that if my son gives this knowledge (to others) without the assent of his preceptor, he will no longer be able to profit by it.

sa: तत्र तत्र महानादैरुत्कृष्टतलनादितैः। यथायोगं यथाप्रीति विजह्वः कुरुवृष्णयः॥
en: The Kurus and the Vrishnis sported there with joyous hearts, often shouting and clapping their hands.

sa: अत्र किंपुरुषीभूत्वा शैलरोधसि वत्स्यथ। आवासस्तु गिरावस्मिञ्शीघ्रमेव विधीयताम्॥
en: Do you all live in this mountain being Kimpurusas; do you make your respective habitations here.

sa: गतायामथ कृष्णायां युधिष्ठिरपुरोगमान्। विविक्ते पाण्डवान् सर्वानुवाच भगवानृपिः॥
en: When Krishna retired, the illustrious Rishi thus spoke to the Pandavas with Yudhishthira at their head.

sa: प्रयाते त्रिदिवे तस्मिन्निक्ष्वाकुरमितप्रभः। जनयिष्ये कथं पुत्रानिति चिन्तापरोऽभवत्॥
en: After Manu's departure towards the heaven, the effulgent Ikşavku thought of the means for creating progeny.

sa: सुमन्त्रस्तु तथेत्युक्त्वा युक्तं परमवाजिभिः। रथं सुरुचिरप्रख्यं स्वास्तीर्णं सुखशय्यया॥ आनीयोवाच सौमित्रिं मित्राणां मानवर्धनम्। रथोऽयं समनुप्राप्तो यत्कार्य क्रियतां प्रभो॥
en: Obeying the mandate, and bringing a beautiful and holy car drawn by first-rate steeds and having excellent seats, he said to Saumitri, the enhancer of friends' honour “O lord, here is the chariot ready-do you now satisfy your desire.

sa: स चैत्ररथमासाद्य कालकूटमतीत्य च। हिमवन्तमतिक्रम्य प्रययौ गन्धमादनम्॥
en: He then went to Chaitraratha and then to Kalakuta. Crossing the Himalayas, he went to Gandhamadana.

sa: वणिम्भिश्चान्वकीर्यन्त नगराण्यथ शिल्पिभिः। शूराश्च कृतविद्याश्च सन्तश्च सुखिनोऽभवन्॥
en: The cities were filled with merchants and artisans; the people became brave, learned, honest and happy.

sa: ऋषयश्च महात्मानः सर्व एव महीसुराः। अन्वगच्छन्महात्मानं स्वर्गद्वारमपावृतम्॥
en: The high-souled Rșis and great Asuras followed the high-souled Rāma to the open gates of heaven.

sa: एवमुक्तस्तु धर्मात्मा शौनकः प्राहसत्तदा। उग्रश्रवसमामन्त्र्य उपपन्नमिति ब्रुवन्॥
en: When the pious Shaunaka heard this, he smiled and addressing Ugrashrava (Sauti) said, “It is true."

sa: प्रतिग्रहश्च वै देयः शृणु यस्य युधिष्ठिर। प्रदातारं तथाऽऽत्मानं यस्तारयति शक्तिमान्॥ तस्मिन् देयं द्विजे दानं सर्वागमविजानता। प्रदातारं यथाऽऽत्मानं तारयेद् यः स शक्तिमान्॥
en: O Yudhishthira, hear now what you should give away. He who knows the Vedas should give away to only those Brahmanas who are able to save both the giver and himself, for he only is to be considered a competent (Brahmana) who can save the giver and himself.

sa: यथेमे पुरुषा नित्यमुत्तमाधममध्यमाः। एवं मन्त्रोऽपि विज्ञेय उत्तमाधममध्यमः॥
en: And counsels are also divided into three divisions like to the three orders of men (mentioned).

sa: भैरीमृदङ्गशङ्खानां दुन्दुभीनां च निःस्वनः। उत्कृष्टसिंहनादैश्च वल्गितैश्च पृथग्विधैः॥
en: With fierce war-dries, and other kinds of shouts, hastily did we advance to meet the foe,

sa: मार्कण्डेय उवाच शृणु राजन् मया दृष्टं यत् पुरा श्रुतमेव च। अनुभूतं च राजेन्द्र देवदेवप्रसादजम्॥
en: Markandeya said : O king, hear all that has been and heard by me and all that has been known to me by intuition through the grace of the god of gods.

sa: सा मुहूर्तमिव ध्यात्वा दुःखामर्षसमन्विता। भर्तारमभिसम्प्रेक्ष्य क्रुद्धा वचनमब्रवीत्॥ जानन्नपि महाराज कस्मादेवं प्रभाषसे। न जानामीति निःशङ्कं यथान्यः प्राकृतो जनः॥
en: Collecting her thought in a moment, she thus addressed her husband looking straight at him in grief and in anger. “O great king, knowing everything, how can you, like a mean and inferior man, say that you know nothing'?

sa: शोकपर्यायसंतप्तः सततं दीर्घमुच्छ्वसन्। अयोध्यायां जनः सर्वश्चक्रोश जगतीपतिम्॥
en: And ceaselessly burning in grief and heaving sighs, the people in Ayodhyā rage at the monarch.

sa: आसनं पूजयामास रामायाभिप्रणम्य च। वालव्यजनमादाय न्यषीदत् सचिवासने॥
en: And then holding the chowri of hair, he sat down on the seat of a minister.

sa: शूद्रकर्म तु यः कुर्यादवहाय स्वकर्म च। स विज्ञेयो यथा शूद्रो न च भोज्य: कदाचन।॥
en: The man who gives up his own proper occupation and does that of a Shudra, should be regarded as a Shudra, and on no account should any food be accepted from him.

sa: स तदा पीडितस्तेन कपिना पर्वतोत्तमः।॥ ररास विविधैर्भूतैः प्राविशद् वसुधातलम्। कम्पमानैश्च शिखरैः पतद्भिरपि च दुमैः॥
en: Then that best of mountains, sore pressed by the monkey, began to emit cries, and with various creatures (on it), entered under the Earth, with its peaks tottering and its trees toppling.

sa: ततस्तूर्यनिनादश्च भेरीणां च महास्वनः। उदितष्ठच राजेन्द्र कर्णभीमसमागमे॥
en: Then there arose, O king, the sound of trumpets and drums when Karna and Bhima met.

sa: स हि वीरः प्रयास्यन् वै धर्मराजेन वारितः। हतबान्धवा न ते पार्थ हन्तव्याः पार्थिवा इति॥
en: At the time of his starting, he had been earnestly ordered by king Yudhishthira the just not to kill those Kshatriyas whose kinsmen had been killed before on the field of Kurukshetra.

sa: शर्मिष्ठोवाच समावेतौ मतौ राजन् पति: सख्याश्च यः पतिः। समं विवाहमित्याहुः सख्या मेऽसि वृतः पतिः॥
en: Sharmishtha said: O king, you have been chosen by my friends as her husband. One's friend's marriage is the same as one's own. You are, therefore, as much my husband (as Devayani's).

sa: अथापराह्णसमये भ्रातृभिः सह राघवः। शुश्राव मधुरां वाणीमन्तरिक्षान्महाप्रभुः॥
en: Thereupon afternoon, Lord Rāghava along with his brothers heard from the air the following sweet accents.

sa: अर्जुन उवाच अयं वै सत्यजिद् राजन्नद्य त्वां रक्षिता युधि। ध्रियमाणे च पाञ्चाल्ये नाचार्यः काममाप्स्यति॥
en: Arjuna said This Satyajit, O monarch, will protect you in battle today; and so long as the prince of the Panchalas lives, the preceptor will not attain the fruition of his desires,

sa: कल्कांश्चूर्णकषायांश्च स्नानानि विविधानि च। ददृशुर्भाजनस्थानि तीर्थेषु सरितां नराः॥ शुक्लानंशुमतश्चापि दन्तधावनसंचयान्। शुक्लांश्चन्दनकल्कांश्च समुद्रेष्ववतिष्ठतः॥ दर्पणान् परिमृष्टांश्च वाससां चापि संचयान्। पादुकोपानहं चैव युग्मान्यत्र सहस्रशः॥ आञ्जनीः कङ्कतान् कूर्चाश्छत्राणि च धनूंषि च। मर्मत्राणानि चित्राणि शयनान्यासनानि च॥
en: And men saw sediments, acrid powders and various others things in vessels, for the purpose of bath, on the terraces of tanks; and toothcleaning sticks of Ansuman and other (trees); and white sandal paste lying before; and cleaned mirros; and lots of cloths; and sandals; and shoes in pairs by thousand; and collyrium-pots; and combs; and brushes; and bows at some places; and mail; and various kinds of seats and beds.

sa: मार्कण्डेय उवाच आपस्य मुदिता भार्या सहस्य परमा प्रिया। भूपतिर्भुवभर्ता च जनयत् पावकं परम्॥ भूतानां चापि सर्वेषां यं प्राहुः पावकं पतिम्। आत्मा भुवनभर्तेति सान्वयेषु द्विजातिषु॥
en: Markandeya said : Mudita, the favourite wife of the fire named Svaha, live in water. Svaha who was the lord of the sky, begot on his that wife a greatly sacred fire named Adbhuta. There is a tradition among the Brahmanas, namely that this fire is the ruler and the inner soul of all creatures.

sa: एवमुक्त्वा ततो रामं संरुध्य भृकुटिं ततः। स ददर्श महासालमविदूरे निशाचरः॥ रणे प्रहरणस्यार्थे सर्वतो ह्यवलोकयन्। स तमुत्पाटयामास संदष्टदशनच्छदम्॥
en: Saying this to Rāma, that ranger of the night (Khara), pursing his brows, espied a mighty Sāla hard by. And looking about him on all sides in the field for a weapon, he uprooted it, biting his Nether lip.

sa: किं करिष्यामि भद्रं वः किं वो युक्तमनन्तरम्। उच्यतां नः समर्थ यत्कृतं च सुकृतं भवेत्॥
en: What shall I do now? And what should you all do one this occasion? It behove you all go give me such counsel as become me and will conduce to my glory.

sa: रथाक्षमात्रा विशिखास्तपनीयविभूषणा॥ कस्येमे निहता वाणाः प्रकीर्णा घोरदर्शनाः।
en: Whose are these terrible arrows feathered in gold, measuring four-hundred fingers, lying without blades on earth?

sa: सत्यवत्यै निवेद्याथ विवाहं समनन्तरम्। भ्रातुर्विचित्रवीर्यस्य समाज्ञापयत प्रभुः॥
en: That lord after submitting the case to Satyavati ordered for the wedding of his brother Vichitravirya.

sa: विद्वान् कूर्म इवाङ्गानि कामान् संहत्य सर्वशः। विरजाः सर्वतो मुक्तो यो नरः स सुखी सदा॥
en: The learned man who takes all desires himself from all sides like thc tortoise withdrawing all its limbs, who is devoid of passion, and who is freed from everything, becoming always happy.

sa: लोकपीडाकरं कर्म न कर्तव्यं विचक्षणैः। बालानां तु शुभं वाक्यं ग्राह्यं लक्ष्मणपूर्वज। तस्माच्छृणोमि ते वाक्यं साधु युक्तं महाबल।।२०
en: The wise should never undertake all those works which give affliction to people. O elder brother of Lakşmaņa, it is proper to take wise counsels even from a boy. O you of great strength, I therefore, hear your speech

sa: दुर्योधनादयः सर्वे ब्राह्मणैः सह संगताः। मृदुपूर्वमयत्नेन प्रत्ययुध्यंस्तदाहवे॥
en: Duryodhana and others all fought with the Brahmanas, but they skirmished with them lightly and carelessly.

sa: स्वल्पं चैव बलं तेषां कृष्णौ च भृशविक्षतौ॥ यदि सर्वेऽत्र तिष्ठामो ध्रुवं नो विजयो भवेत्।
en: The Pandava army has now been reduced to a small number. The two Krishna have been greatly wounded. If all of us make a stand here, we are sure to gain victory.

sa: ततो देवगणान् सर्वांस्तपसाहं प्रसादयम्॥ ददुश्च परमप्रीताश्चतुरङ्गबलं सुराः।
en: Then I sought to propitiate the deities; and well-pleased, the celestials granted me a Caturanga army.

sa: सर्वेषामनुरूपाश्च कृता दारा महीपते। धृतराष्ट्रेण समये परीक्ष्य विधिवत्रुप॥ दुःशलां चापि समये धृतराष्ट्रो नराधिपः। जयद्रथाय प्रददौ विधिना भरतर्षभ॥
en: O king, worthy wives were selected for them at the proper time and after due examinations by king Dhritarashtra. O best of the Bharata race, king Dhritarashtra bestowed Dushala at the proper time and with due rites on Jayadratha.

sa: द्वारेषु तासां चत्वारः संक्रमाः परमायताः। यन्त्रैरुपेता बहुभिर्महद्भिर्गृहपङ्क्तिभिः॥
en: At the gates are four broad bridges, furnished with machines and many rows of grand structures.

sa: सात्यकि शरवर्षेण छादयामासुरोजसा। स च्छाद्यमानो बहुभिस्तव पुत्रैर्महारथैः॥
en: Covered Satyaki with a shower of mighty arrows. Thus covered by your sons, all mighty car-warriors.

sa: वलयैश्छादयिष्यामि बाहू किणकृताविमौ। कर्णयोः प्रतिमुच्याहं कुण्डले ज्वलनप्रभे॥
en: However, I shall conceal with the bangles the marks of my arm caused by the bow-string.

sa: ततस्तान् हरिवृद्धांश्च तच्च सैन्यमरिंदमः। अनुमान्याङ्गदः श्रीमान् वाक्यमर्थवदब्रवीत्॥
en: Then saluting the elders as well as army, the-graceful Angada-repressor of foes-~-spoke words fraught with sense,

sa: श्येन उवाच न वराहं न चोक्षाणं न मृगान् विविधांस्तथा। भक्षयामि महाराज किं ममान्येन केनचित्॥
en: The Hawk said: O great king, I am not desirous of eating a boar or an ox or any other kind of beasts. What have I to do with any other food?

sa: ततोऽब्रवीनृपो वाक्यं ब्राह्मणान् वेदपारगान्॥ सुमन्त्रावाहय क्षिप्रमृत्विजो ब्रह्मवादिनः। सुयज्ञं वामदेवं च जाबालिमथ काश्यपम्॥ पुरोहितं वसिष्ठं च ये चान्ये द्विजसत्तमाः।
en: Then the king spoke to Sumantra, saying, O Sumantra, do you summon speedily Brāhmaṇas versed in the Vedas and priests professing the Vedānta philosophy, Suyajña, and Vāmadeva, and Jabali, and Kasyapa, and the priest Vasistha, together with other excellent twice-born ones.

sa: युधिष्ठिर उवाच असंतोषः प्रमादश्च मदो रागोऽप्रशान्तता। बलं मोहोऽभिमानश्चाप्युद्वेगश्चैव सर्वशः॥ एभिः पाप्मभिराविष्टो राज्यं त्वमभिकाङ्क्षसे। निरामिषो विनिर्मुक्तः प्रशान्तः सुसुखी भव॥
en: Yudhishthira said Visited by the sins of discontent, heedlessness, attachment to earthly objects, the absence of tranquillity, power, folly, vanity, and anxiety, O Bhima, you covet sovereignty. Freed from desire, overcoming joy and grief and acquiring tranquillity, try to be happy.

sa: अपत्यं नाम लोकेषु प्रतिष्ठा धर्मसंहिता। इति कुन्ति विदुर्धीराः शाश्वतं धर्मवादिनः॥ इष्टं दत्तं तपस्तप्तं नियमश्च स्वनुष्ठितः। सर्वमेवानपत्यस्य न पावनमिहोच्यते॥
en: O Kunti, the wise expounders of the eternal religion say that son is the source of virtuous fame in the three worlds, Sacrifices, gifts in charity, ascetic penances and carefully observed vows, do not free a sonless man from his sins.

sa: वायुसूनोर्बलेनैव दग्धा लङ्केति नः श्रुतम् ॥ दृष्ट्वा देवी न चानीता इति तत्र निवेदितुम्। न युक्तमिव पश्यामि भवद्भिः ख्यातपौरुषैः॥
en: I have heard, that, by Wind-god's son alone Lankā was burnt. You are all famed for your manliness, it dose not behove you to speak before Rāma. “We have seen the worshipful dame but have not been able to bring her.'

sa: दुर्योधनमिदं वाक्यमब्रवीद् युद्धलालसः। विदितं ते महाराज यथा भीमेन राक्षसाः॥ हिडिम्बबककिर्मीरा निहता मम बान्धवाः। परामर्शश्च कन्याया हिडिम्बायाः कृतः पुरा॥
en: That one longing to engage in the fight spoke these words addressing Duryodhana "O mighty monarch, you have heard how Bhima slew my relatives the Rakshasas Vaka, Krimira and Hidimba in battle. In days gone by, he ravished our daughter Hidimba.

sa: भीष्म उवाच पुनर्भरतवंशस्य हेतुं संतानवृद्धये। वक्ष्यामि नियतं मातस्तन्मे निगदतः शृणु॥ ब्राह्मणो गुणवान् कश्चिद् धनेनोपनिमन्त्र्यताम्। विचित्रवीर्यक्षेत्रेषु यः समुत्पादयेत् प्रजाः॥
en: Bhishma said: O mother, listen to me, I shall point out the means by which the Bharata dynasty may be perpetuated. Let an accomplished Brahmana be invited with the offer of wealth; let him beget offspring on the wives of Vichitravirya.

sa: आनन्दः प्रीतिरुद्रेक: प्रकाश्यं सुखमेव च। अकार्पण्यमसंरम्भः सन्तोष: श्रद्दधानता॥ क्षमा धृतिरहिंसा च समता सत्यमार्जवम्। अक्रोधश्चानसूया च शौचं दाक्ष्यं पराक्रमः॥
en: Joy, satisfaction, nobility, enlightenment, and happiness, absence of stinginess, absence of fear, contentment, disposition for faith, forgiveness, courage, abstention from injuring any creature, equability, truth, straightforwardness, absence of anger, absence of malice, purity, cleverness, prowess, belong to the quality of Goodness.

sa: विपुल उवाच ब्रह्मर्षे मिथुनं किं तत् के च ते पुरुषा विभो। ये मां जानन्ति तत्त्वेन यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि।॥
en: Vipula said O twiceborn Rishi, who are those two whom I first saw? Who also are those other six whom I saw afterwards? All of them know me. Who indeed, are they to whom you prefer in your speech to me?

sa: त्वं तु सौम्य परित्रस्तो हरिभिः पीडितो भृशम्। प्रतिप्रदानमद्यैव सीतायाः साधु मन्यसे॥ को हि नाम सपत्नो मां समरे जेतुमर्हति।
en: O amiable one, you, having been hard handled by the monkeys and distressed in consequence, deems it fit that Sītā should be rendered back this very day. What foe of mine is there who is competent to conquer me in battle?

sa: तस्याङ्गदः सरोषाक्षो राक्षसस्य तमायसम्। दूरस्थितस्य परिघं रविरश्मिसमप्रभम्॥ द्वाभ्यां भुजाभ्यां संगृह्या भ्रामयित्वा च वेगवत्। महापार्थाय चिक्षेप वधार्थं वालिनः सुतः॥
en: Holding with two hands that parigha made of iron and bright like the rays of the sun, Angada, the son of Vāli, with his eyes reddened in wrath, hurled it at Mahāpārsva who was stationed at a distance, to slay him.

sa: तानि नागसहस्राणि सारोहाणि च वाजिनाम्। रथानां त्वग्निवर्णानां सध्वजानां सहस्रशः॥ राक्षसानां सहस्राणि गदापरिघयोधिनाम्। काञ्चनध्वजचित्राणां शूराणां कामरूपिणाम्॥ निहतानि शरैर्दीपैस्तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणैः। रावणेन प्रयुक्तानि रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा॥ दृष्ट्वा श्रुत्वा च संभ्रान्ता हतशेषा निशाचराः। राक्षस्यश्च समागम्य दीनाश्चिन्तापरिप्लुताः॥
en: By Rāma of unwearied actions, with flaming arrows feathered in burning gold, were destroyed thousands of elephants-many horses with their riders, many a car crested with flaming banners; thousands of heroic Rákşasas assuming shapes at will engaged by Råvana, and armed with clubs and parighas; and golden pennons. Beholding and hearing of this the remaining night-rangers assembled and were greatly bewildered, poorly and stricken with anxiety.

sa: यथास्तं गत आदित्ये नावतिष्ठन्ति रश्मयः। तथा तस्मिन्निपतिते राक्षसास्ते गता दिशः ८१॥ शान्तरश्मिरिवादित्यो निर्वाण इव पावकः। बभूव स महाबाहुर्व्यपास्तगतजीवितः॥
en: As when the Sun sets, his rays remain no longer, on that Raksasas having fallen, the Raks asas dispersed in the ten cardinal quarters, like to the sun when his rays have been rendered mild, or fire which has been extinguished.

sa: जग्राह तरसा सीतां ग्रहः खे रोहिणीमिव। त्रातुकामं ततो युद्धे हत्वा गृधं जटायुषम्॥ प्रगृह्य सहसा सीतां जगामाशु स राक्षसः।
en: And he speedily got hold of Sītā, like to Rohiņi possessed by the planet in the sky. Thereupon slaying the vulture Jatayu in the conflict desirous of rescuing her and getting hold of Sītā that Rākşasa speedily repaired (to his capital).

sa: ततो मुहूर्तानिष्पेतू राक्षसा भीमदर्शनाः। नदन्तो भीमवदना नानाप्रहरणैर्भुजैः॥ असिभिः पट्टिशैः शूलैर्गदाभिर्मुसलैर्हलैः। शक्तिभिस्तीक्ष्णधाराभिर्महद्भिः कूटमुद्गरैः॥ यष्टिभिर्विविधैश्च निशितैश्च परश्वधैः। भिन्दिपालैः शतघ्नीभिरन्यैश्चापि वरायुधैः॥
en: Thereupon began to issue out in a moment terrible-looking Raksasas, emitting roars, having dreadful faces and with various weapons in their hands-daggers, Pattisas, maces, clubs, furrows, sharpened Śaktis, traps, various rods, sharpened Cakra, Parasvadhas, Bhindipālas, Sataghnis and various other excellent weapons.

sa: माल्यवान् नाम वैदेहि गिरिणामुत्तमो गिरिः । ७९ ।। ततो गच्छति गोकर्ण पर्वतं केसरी हरिः। स च देवर्षिभिर्दिष्टः पिता मम महाकपिः।। तीर्थे नदीपतेः पुण्ये शम्बसादनमुद्धरन्॥ यस्याहं हरिणः क्षेत्रे जातो वातेन मैथिलि। हनूमानिति विख्यातो लोके स्वेनैव कर्मणा ॥
en: There is a hill, O Vaidehi, named Malyavana, the foremost of all the mountains. There lives my father, the great monkey Kesari. Being commanded by the celestial ascetics, he once repaired thence to the mount Gokarna and at the holy watering place of the lord of the rivers he brought about the destruction of (the Asura) Sammasādana. O Vaidehi, I was bom, on the field, of that monkey. And I am known all over the world as Hanumān by my own actions.

sa: प्रस्थितो दक्षिणामाशां प्रविष्टोऽकर्दमं हृदम्। कण्ठे बद्ध्वा दशग्रीवं प्रमदा रक्तवासिनी॥ कालीकर्दमलिप्ताङ्गी दिशं याम्यां प्रकर्षति। एवं तत्र मया दृष्टः कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः॥ रावणस्य सुताः सर्वे मुण्डास्तैलसमुक्षिताः। वराहेण दशग्रीवं शिशुमारेण चेन्द्रजित्॥ उष्ट्रेण कुम्भकर्णश्च प्रयातो दक्षिणां दिशम्।
en: And a dark woman, clad in a crimson cloth, and bedaubed with mud, dragged the Ten-necked demon, entwining herself around his neck. Then followed the mighty Kumbhakarņa (Rāvana's brother) and all the sons of Rāvana, shaved and shorn and besmeared with oil. And they all proceeded southward—the Ten-necked demon on a boar, Indrajit (Rāvana's son-the name signifies the conqueror of the lord of the celestials) on a porpoise, and Kumbhakarņa on a camel.

sa: रामस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा ऋक्षवानरराक्षसाः। साधुसाध्विति काकुत्स्थं प्रशशंसुः पुनः पुनः॥ तव बुद्धिर्महाबाहो वीर्यमद्भुतमेव च। माधुर्यं परमं राम स्वयंभोरिव नित्यदा॥
en: Hearing the words of Rama, the bears, monkeys and Rākşasas repeatedly exclaimed glory to Rāma and said. 'O Rāma, having long arms, your understanding resemble that of the Self-Sprung, your prowess is equally wonderful and your beauty is also par excellence.”

sa: समीक्ष्य स्वबलं संख्ये वरुणस्य सुतास्तदा। अर्दिताः शरजालेन निवृत्ता रणकर्मणः॥ महीतलगतास्ते तु रावणं दृश्य पुष्पके। आकाशमाशु विविशुः स्यन्दनैः शीघ्रगामिभिः॥
en: Seeing their own forces brought to straits in the conflict and driven back in the fight with networks of shafts, and down on the ground and seeing Rävaņa in Puspaka, Varuņa's sons swiftly shot into the welkin with their fleet-footing cars.

sa: यस्यां स्तम्भसहस्रेण प्रासादः समलंकृतः। कैलासशिखराकारो दृश्यते खमिवोल्लिखन्।।२२ चैत्यः स राक्षसेन्द्रस्य बभूव पुरभूषणम्। शतेन रक्षसां नित्यं यः समग्रेण रक्ष्यते॥
en: That palace, which was adorned with thousands of pillars, and which, as if piercing the heavens, looked like a peak of Kailasa—was the residence of the Sovereign of the Rākşasas—the ornament of the city, (ever guarded by full hundreds of Raksasas.

sa: तस्मिन्प्रतिहतेऽस्त्रे तु रावणो राक्षसाधिपः। क्रोधं च द्विगुणं चक्रे क्रोधाच्चास्त्रमनन्तरम्॥ मयेन विहितं रौद्रमन्यदस्त्रं महाद्युतिः। उत्स्रष्टुं रावणो भीमं राघवाय प्रचक्रमे॥
en: On that weapon of his hvaing been baffled, Rāvaņa lord of the Rākṣasas-was fired with double fury, and the highly effuigent Rāvaņa from wrath set about discharging at Rāghava a dreadful Rudra weapon, which had been। conferred on him by Maya.

sa: व्यास उवाच न कर्मणा लभ्यते चिन्तया वा नाप्यस्ति दाता पुरुषस्य कश्चित्। पर्याययोगाद् विहितं विधात्रा कालेन सर्वं लभते मनुष्यः॥
en: Vyasa said, No one can acquire anything by his own deeds or by sacrifices and adoration. No man can give anything to another. Man gets everything through Time. The Great Ordainer has made the course of Time the instrument of acquisition.

sa: मन्त्रश्च वर्णितः कृत्स्नस्तथा भेदार्थ एव च। विभ्रमश्चैव मन्त्रस्य सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योश्च यत् फलम्॥ संधिश्च त्रिविधाभिख्यो हीनो मध्यस्तथोत्तमः। भयसत्कारवित्ताख्यं कात्स्येन परिवर्णितम्॥
en: Deliberation of all sorts, counsels for creating disunion, the mistakes of deliberation, the results of the success or failure of counsels of three kinds viz., bad, middling, and good, made through fear, good conduct and gifts of wealth, were described there.

sa: उन्मत्ताश्च विचेष्टन्ते नष्टसंज्ञा विचेतसः॥ स्वपन्ति च प्लवन्ते च छर्दयन्ति च मानवाः। मूत्रयन्ते च सततं रुदन्ति च हसन्ति च॥
en: By using these weapons men, struck with them, move about intoxicated, taking leave of their senses and with their minds bewildered. When pierced by them, men sleep, move about here and there, pass excrete and urine and always weep and laugh,

sa: प्राज्ञो वा कुरुवृद्धोऽयं सर्वेषां नः पितामहः। आचार्यश्च यथा द्रोणः कृपः शारद्वतस्तथा। मन्यन्ते ते यथा सर्वे तथा यात्रा विधीयताम्॥
en: Or so arrange the expedition, as is liked by Sharadvata's son Kripa, the preceptor Drona and the wise and the aged grand-father of the Kurus; O king of the earth, consulting with each other we shall speedily start to gainour end.

sa: समाहूतो निवर्तेत प्राणत्यागेऽप्युपस्थिते। अधर्मेण जितान् दृष्ट्वा वने प्रव्रजितांस्तथा॥ वध्यतां मम वार्ष्णेय निर्गतोऽसौ सुयोधनः। न चैतदद्भुतं कृष्ण मित्रार्थं यच्चिकीर्षसि। क्रिया कथं च मुख्या स्यान्मृदुना चेतरेण वा॥
en: Did I think that Suyodhana ought to be slain by me when I came out of the forest, O you of the Vrishini race; but what you desire to do on behalf of your friends is not strange, O Krishna, though how that is capable of accomplishment by mildness or by other means (I do not see).

sa: भानुमन्ति विचित्राणि शूरसेव्यानि भागशः। सवज्रायसग तु कवचं तत्र काञ्चनम्॥ विराटस्य प्रियो भ्राता शतानीकोऽभ्यहारयत्। सर्वपारसवं वर्म कल्याणपटलं दृढम्॥ शतानीकादवरजो मदिराक्षोऽभ्यहारयत्। शतसूर्यं शतावर्ती शतबिन्दु शताक्षिमत्॥ अभेद्यकल्पं मत्स्यानां राजा कवचमाहरत्। उत्सेधे यस्य पद्मानि शतं सौगन्धिकानि च॥ सुवर्णपृष्ठं सूर्याभं सूर्यदत्तोऽभ्यहारयत्। दृढमायसगर्भं च श्वेतं वर्म शताक्षिमत्॥ विराटस्य सुतो ज्येष्ठो वीरः शङ्खोऽभ्यहारयत्। शतशश्च तनुत्राणि यथास्वं ते महारथाः॥ योत्स्यमाना अनह्यन्त देवरूपाः प्रह
en: Brilliant, variegated and worthy of being worn by heroes according to their respective divisions. Virata's beloved brother Shatanika put on an armour made of adamant and adorned with gold. Madiraksha, next born to Shatanika, put on a strong armour plaited with gold and capable of withstanding every weapon. The armour, which the king of Matsya's himself wore, invincible, adorned with a hundred suns, a hundred was circles, a hundred spots, and a hundred eyes. The armour, that Suryadatta put on, was radiant like the sun, plaited with gold and broad like a hundred fragrant lotuses. The one, that Virata's eldest son Sankasha put on, was invulnerable, inade of burnished steel and adorned with a hundred golden eyes. In this way hundreds of god-like and powerful heroes, mighty carwarriors, adorned

sa: लोमपादश्च राजर्षिः शान्तां दत्त्वा सुतां प्रभुः। ऋष्य शृङ्गाय विपुलैः सर्वकामैरयुज्यत॥ मदिराश्वश्च राजर्षिर्दत्त्वा कन्यां सुमध्यमाम्। हिरण्यहस्ताय गतो लोकान् देवैरभिष्टुतान्॥
en: By giving away daughter Shanta to Rishyarshringa, the highly powerful royal sage Lomapada obtained the fruition of all his wishes. By giving away his slender waisted daughter of Hiranyahasta, the royal sage Madirashva, ascended to regions esteemed of the very gods.

sa: प्राच्छादयन्महाराज दिशः सूर्यस्य च प्रभाः। ततः कनकपुड्वानां शराणां नतपर्वणाम्॥ धनुश्च्युतानां वियति ददृशे बहुधा व्रजः। बाणासनादाधिरथेः प्रभवन्ति स्म सायकाः॥
en: Covered, () monarch, all the quarters, intercepting the very rays of the solar orb. In the skies then were seen numerous groups of shafts, furnished with golden wings and shot from the bow of Karna. The arrows discharged from Karna's bow.

sa: अयोधयन् रणे शूराः सात्वतं युद्धदुर्मदम्। तांस्तु सर्वान् स बलवान् सात्यकियुद्धदुर्मदः॥ नातिकृच्छ्राद्धसन्नेव विजिग्ये पुरुषर्षभः। मागधान् द्रवतो दृष्ट्वा हतशेषान् समन्ततः॥
en: Those heroes fought on with the invincible Satvata hero, in battle. Then indomitable Satyaki, that foremost of men endued with great strength without the slightest difficulty, smiling the while vanquished the Magadhas and the few that survived, fled in all directions.

sa: गजान् सकङ्कटान् मत्तान् सारोहान् सपताकिनः। पततः समपश्याम सपक्षान् पर्वतानिव॥ हत्वा तु तदु गजानीकं भीमसेनो महाबलः। पुनः स्वरथमास्थाय पृष्ठतोऽर्जुनमभ्ययात॥
en: We could see the furious elephants cased in mail, with riders and banners, tumbling down on all sides like so many winged mountains and the powerful Bhimasena thus exterminating the elephant division went back to his car and joined Arjuna's rear.

sa: ध्वजमेकेन बाणेन विव्याध युधि मारिष। तं द्रोण: साश्वयन्तारं सरथध्वजमाशुगैः॥ त्वरन् प्राच्छादयद् बाणैः शलभानामिव व्रजैः। तथैव युयुधानोऽपि द्रोणं बहुभिराशुगैः॥
en: O sire in that battle, he pierced Drona's standard with another arrows. Thereupon Drona quickly discharging his swift-flying arrows that resembled fights of locusts, covered Satyaki together with his steeds, charioteer, chariot and standard. So also Yuyudhana with countless swift-coursing shafts.

sa: सहस्राणि दशाश्वानां हत्वा पत्तींश्च भूयसा। भीमोऽभ्यधावत् संक्रुद्धो गदापाणिरितस्ततः॥ गदापाणिं ततो भीमं दृष्ट्वा भारत तावकाः। मेनिरे समनुप्राप्तं कालदण्डोद्यतं यमम्॥
en: Bhima slaughtered ten thousand horse and numberless infantry and was running to and fro in wrath, with mace in hand; and your troops, O Bharata, seeing him thought that the Pluto himself has come among them, armed with his death-dealing wand.

sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्त्वा स नृपः शोचन निषसाद महीतले। यात्मरतो विद्वाञ्छौनको नाम वै द्विजः॥ योगे सांख्ये च कुशलो राजानमिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having said this, that king (Yudhishthira) sat down weeping on the ground. Then a learned Brahmana, named Shaunaka, who was learned in the philosophy of the soul and in the Sankhya and Yoga, thus spoke to the king.

sa: द्रोणस्य शरजालानि प्राणिदेहहराणि च। षडरनि धनुश्चास्य दृश्यते परमं महत्॥ स हि ब्राह्मणवेषेण क्षात्रं वेगमसंशयम्। प्रतिहन्ति महेष्वासो भारद्वाजो महामनाः॥
en: His arrows are capable of killing every living being, his bow is full six cubits long and it looks exceedingly great. That high-souled ' great bowman, that son of Bharadvaja (Drona,) attired in the Brahmanic garb, is destroying the Kshatriya might.

sa: धर्ममेवं जनाः सन्तः पुराणं परिचक्षते। भर्ता भार्यां राजपुत्रि धर्म्य वाधर्म्यमेव वा॥ यद् ब्रूयात् तत् तथा कार्यमिति वेदविदो विदुः।
en: The wise have said that this was the ancient practice. But, O princess, men, learned in the Vedas, have declared that whether the act be sinful or sinless, it is the duty of the wife to do what her husband commands.

sa: इत्येते देवगन्धर्वाः प्राधायाः परिकीर्तिताः। मं त्वप्सरसां वंशं विदितं पुण्यलक्षणम्॥ प्राधाऽसूत महाभागा देवी देवर्षितः पुरा। अलम्बुषा मिश्रकेशी विद्युत्पर्णा तिलोत्तमा॥
en: These Devas and Gandharvas were also known to be the progeny of Pradha. It is also known that, that lady of good fortune Pradha, through the celestial Rishi (Kashyapa), brought forth the holy race of Apsaras, namely, Alambusha. Mishrakeshi, Vidyutaparna, Tilottama,

sa: यथैव पाण्डवा भूमौ सुषुपुः सह बान्धवैः। तथैव नागरा राजन् शिश्यिरे ब्राह्मणादयः॥ तद्गतानन्दमस्वस्थमाकुमारमहष्टवत्। बभूव पाण्डवैः सार्धं नगरं द्वादश क्षपाः॥
en: The Pandavas slept on the ground with their friends and relatives. O king, seeing this the Brahmanas and other citizens also gave their bed. Young and old, all men grieved with the sons of Pandu and passed twelve days in mourning.

sa: दास्यामि हि वरं तेऽद्य प्रीतिर्मेपरमा त्वयि। दिष्ट्या बुद्धिश्च ते धर्मे निविष्टा पन्नगोत्तम। भूयो भूयश्च ते बुद्धिर्धर्मे भवतु सुस्थिरा॥
en: I am highly pleased with you and I shall grant you a boon today. O best of snakes, it is very good that your heart has been set on virtue. Let your heart be more and more firmly set on virtue."

sa: स्त्र्युवाच त्वं वेत्स्यसे मामिह यास्मि शक्र चदर्थं चाहं रोदिमि मन्दभाग्या। आगच्छ राजन् पुरतो गमिष्ये द्रष्टासि तद् रोदिमि यत्कृतेऽहम्॥
en: The Lady said : O Shakra, unfortunate as I am, you may know who I am and why I am I weeping. O king, if you come with me as I lead the way, you can then see why I weep.

sa: भवन्तः सुहृदोऽस्माकमस्मान् कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणम्। प्रतिनन्द्य तथाशीभिर्निवर्तध्वं यथा गृहम्॥ यदा तु कार्यमस्माकं भवद्भिपपत्स्यते। तदा करिष्यथास्माकं प्रियाणि च हितानि च॥
en: "You are our friends; walking round us and making us happy with your blessings, return to your homes. When the time comes for anything to be done for us by you, then accomplish all that is agreeable and beneficial to us."

sa: उदीच्याश्च तथा भोजाः कुलान्यष्टादश प्रभो। जरासंधभयादेव प्रतीची दिशमास्थिताः॥ शूरसेना भद्रकारा बोधाः शाल्वाः पटच्चराः। सुस्थलाश्च सुकुटाश्च कुलिन्दाः कुन्तिभिः सह॥
en: O lord, the eighteen tribes of the Bhojas from the fear of Jarasandha, have fled to the west; so also have fled the Shurasenas, the Bhadrakas, the Bodhas, the Shalvas, the patachharas, the Susthalas the Sukuttas, the Kulindas and the Kuntis.

sa: द्वौ पुत्रौ विनतायास्तु विख्यातौ गरुडारुणौ। इत्येषः सर्वभूतानां महतां मनुजाधिप॥ प्रभवः कीर्तितः सम्यङ्मया मतिमतांवर॥ यं श्रुत्वा पुरुषः सम्यङ्मुक्तो भवति पाप्मनः। सर्वज्ञतां च लभते गतिमग्र्यं च विन्दति॥
en: Vinata had two sons, the world known Garuda and Aruna. O king of men, O best of all wise men, thus have I fully described to you the genealogy of all the principal creatures. He who hears it is cleansed of all his sins. He acquires great knowledge and finally attains to the highest state in after-life.

sa: तस्याश्वो व्यचरद् भूमिं पुत्रैः स परिरक्षितः। समुद्रं स समासाद्य निस्तोयं भीमदर्शनम्॥ रक्ष्यमाणः प्रयत्नेन तत्रैवान्तरधीयत। ततस्ते सागरास्तात हृतं मत्वा हयोत्तमम्॥ आगम्य पितुराचख्युरदृश्यं तुरगं हृतम्। तेनोक्ता दिक्षु सर्वासु सर्वे मार्गत वाजिनम्॥
en: His horse, guarded by his sons, roamed over the world. Going to the fearful and waterless ocean. It disappeared there, though it was guarded with all care. O child, they thought that the excellent horse had been robbed. Going (back) to their father, they told him how the horse had disappeared and had been stolen. He (Sagara) said, “Go and search the horse in all directions."

sa: स विज्ञेयः पुरुषोऽन्यत्रकामो निन्दाप्रशंसे हि तथा युनक्ति। जिह्वा कथं ते हृदयं व्यनक्ति यो न ज्यायसः कृथा मनसः प्रातिकूल्यम्॥
en: That man who wishes for the success of those that are dear to him and defeat of those that are not dear to him stands confessed. He is known by his praise and blame. Your tongue and mind betray your heart.

sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तस्य मार्कण्डेयस्यधीमतः॥ संहृष्टाः पाण्डवा राजन् सहिताः शाईधन्वना। विप्रर्षभाच ते सर्वे ये तत्रासन् समागताः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having heard the words of the intelligent Markandeya. O king, the Pandavas became exceedingly glad along with the wielder of the (bow) Sharnga (Krishna) and with all those foremost of Brahmanas and with all those that were there.

sa: यदा हि पूर्वं निकृतो निकृन्तेद् वैरं सपुष्पं सफलं विदित्वा। महागुणं हरति हि पौरुषेण तदा वीरो जीवति जीवलोके॥ श्रियं च लोके लभते समग्रां मन्ये चास्मै शत्रवः संनमन्ते। मित्राणि चैनमचिराद् भजन्ते देवा इवेन्द्रमुपजीवन्ति चैनम्॥
en: When one that has been first injured succeeds in revenging himself upon his enemy at a time when the latter's enmity has borne fruits and flowers, he is regarded as one who has accomplished a great deed by his prowess. Such a brave man earns undying fame. Such a man obtains great prosperity. His enemies bow down to him and his friends gather round him, as the celestials cluster round Indra for protection.

sa: मेरुं प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा सम्प्रयात्युत्तरान् कुरून्।॥ तत्र तेषां मन:शान्तिन पिपासा जनाधिप। तस्मिन् फलरसे पीते न जरा बाधते च तान्॥ तत्र जाम्बूनदं नाम कनकं देवभूषणम्। इन्द्रगोपकसंकाशं जायते भास्वरं तु तत्॥ तरुणादित्यवर्णाश्च जायन्ते तत्र मानवाः।
en: Passing round the Meru mountains comes to the country of the northern Kurus. If that juice is drunk, it gives peace of mind. No thirst is ever after felt. O king, old age never comes. A kind of gold called Jambunada is also produced there. They are used in making celestial weapons. They are very shining and look like the Indragopaka insccts. The men born there possess the complexion of the morning sun.

sa: संजय उवाच व्यूढानां उभयोः सेनयोस्तत्र योधा जहषिरे तदा। स्रजः समाः सुगन्धानामुभयत्र समुद्भवः॥ संहतानामनीकानां भरतर्षभ। संसर्गात् समुदीर्णानां विमर्दः सुमहानभूत्॥
en: Sanjaya said The warriors of both the armies were cheerful in the beginning. The garlands of flowers and unguents emitted equal fragrance. O best of the Bharata race, fearful was the encounter that took place between the troops arrayed for battle.

sa: प्रसीद लङ्केश्वर राक्षसेन्द्र लङ्कां प्रसन्नो भव साधु गच्छ। त्वं स्वेषु दारेषु रमस्व नित्यं रामः सभार्यो रमतां वनेषु ॥
en: Be propitious, O lord of Lankā! O foremost of Rākşasas, with a contented heart, you had better go your way to Lankā. Do you ever sport with your own wives: let Rāma in company with his wife, sport in the woods.

sa: ददामि ते रोहिणीनां सहस्रं प्रियो हि मे ब्राह्मणो याचमानः। न मे मनः कुप्यति याचमाने दत्तं न शोचामि कदाचिदर्थम्॥
en: I shall give you one thousand kine; the Brahmana who asks me for a gift is always very dear to me. I am never angry with a man who asks of me and I am never sorry for having given away.

sa: सहदेवस्ततो विद्वान् निपपात महीतले। तं चापि पतितं दृष्ट्वा भीमो राजानमब्रवीत्॥ योऽयमस्मासु सर्वेषु शुश्रूषुरनहंकृतः। सोऽयं माद्रवतीपुत्रः कस्मान् निपतितो भुवि॥
en: Then the all wise Sahadeva dropped down on the Earth. Seeing him drop down. Bhima addressed the king. saying, 'He who with great humility used to serve us all, alas, why is that son of Madravati fallen down on the Earth?'

sa: तेन त्यक्ताश्रयो बाणाः शिताः शत्रुनिवर्हणाः। विकृष्य सुमहच्चापं सुपर्णानिलतुल्यगाः॥ ते बाणा वज्रसंकाशाः सुघोरा रक्तभोजनाः। आजग्मुः सहिताः सर्वे त्रयः संनतपर्वणः॥
en: Then stringing his huge bow he darted three sharpened arrows at me. Those three terrible arrows with bent knots resembling thunderbolts, killing enemies and drinking blood and having the motion of Garuda and air, coalescing with each other came before us.

sa: सर्वभूतान् प्रति यथा तपन: शिशिरात्यये। स विजित्य गृहीत्वा च नृपतीन् राजसत्तमः॥ प्राच्यानुदीच्या पाश्चान्यान् दाक्षिणात्यानकालयत्। अश्वमेधे महायज्ञे व्युषिताश्वः प्रतापवान्॥
en: O king, thereupon Vyushitashva began to shine over all creatures like the sun after the season of frost. O best of kings, he conquered all the monarchs of the east, west, north and south and he exacted tribute from them all.

sa: किमर्थमहमादृत्य त्वया राजप्रबोधितः॥ शंस कस्माद्भयं तेऽत्र को वा प्रेतो भविष्यति। भ्रातरं रावणः क्रुद्धं कुम्भकर्णमवस्थितम्।। रोषेण परिवृत्ताभ्यां नेत्राभ्यां वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: O king, why honouring me, has you awaked me? Tell me whence springs your fear? And who shall be a ghost?* Thereat Ravana, waxing wroth, and with his eyes rolling in rage, said to Kumbhakarma, seated. *Having been slain by me.

sa: तीर्थं तत्र महाराज श्वाविल्लोमापहं स्मृतम्। यत्र विप्रा नरव्याघ्र विद्वांसस्तीर्थतत्पराः॥ प्रीतिं गच्छन्ति परमां स्नात्वा भरतसत्तम। वाविल्लोमापनयने तीर्थे भरतसत्तम॥ प्राणायामैर्निर्हरन्ति स्वलोमानि द्विजोत्तमाः। पूतात्मानश्च राजेन्द्र प्रयान्ति परमां गतिम्॥
en: O great king, in that spot there is a Tirtha called Shvaillomapaha. O foremost of men, learned Brahmanas who always visit Tirthas. Get great pleasure by bathing in it. O best of the Bharata race, shaving their heads at the Shvaillomapaha Tirtha, the excellent Brahmanas acquire holiness by Pranayama; and becoming pure-souled they obtain the highest state.

sa: त्वामहं सत्यमिच्छामि नानृतं पुरुषर्षभ। प्रत्यक्षं तव सत्येन सुकृतेन च ते शपे॥ न च शक्यं मया तात स्थातुं क्षणमपि प्रभो। स शोकं धारयस्वेमं नहि मेऽस्ति विपर्ययः॥
en: O foremost of men, all I wish for is that you may not come by falsehood, and abide by truth. I truly and in good sooth swear before you that I cannot, O lord, remain here for a moment longer, O my father. Do you bear this grief. I cannot for certain act contrary to my promise.

sa: ततः प्रीतमना राजा प्राप्य यज्ञमनुत्तमम्॥ पापापहं स्वर्नयनं दुस्तरं पार्थिवर्षभैः। ततोऽब्रवीदृष्यशृङ्ग राजा दशरथस्तदा॥ कुलस्य वर्धनं तत् तु कर्तुमर्हसि सुव्रत।
en: Then having celebrated that excellent and sindestroying sacrifice, bringing heaven, and incapable of being celebrated by foremost monarchs, king Dasaratha, well pleased, spoke to Rsyasriga, saying, Oyou of excellent vows, it behove you to do that whereby my line may increase.

sa: निर्यातयितुमिच्छामि तच्च वैरं महारिपोः। नहि लप्स्याम्यहं निद्रामहत्वा संयुगे रिपुम्॥ तं त्विदानीमहं हत्वा खरदूषणघातिनम्। राम शर्मोपलप्स्यामि धनं लब्ध्वेव निर्धनः॥
en: I wish to avenge myself on my mighty enemy. Sleep find I none without slaying my foe in fight. Slaying that slayer of Khara and Dūşaņa, Rāma, I shall attain delight like to that attained by a pauper on gaining riches.

sa: न चासौ रक्षसां योग्यः कूटयुद्धा हि राक्षसाः। विप्रयुक्तो हि रामेण मुहूर्तमपि नोत्सहे॥ जीवितुं मुनिशार्दूल न रामं नेतुमर्हसि। यदि वा राघवं ब्रह्मन् नेतुमिच्छसि सुव्रत॥ चतुरङ्गसमायुक्तं मया सह च तं नय।
en: He is not a match for Räkşasas,-they being deceitful warriors. Bereft of Rāma, O tiger among ascetics, I cannot live for a moment. Therefore, it behove you not to take him. If, O Brahman, it is your intention to take Rāma, then O you of excellent vows, do you also take me along with the Caturanga forces! (An army consisting of foot, horse, elephants, and cars.)

sa: स सर्वाश्च दिशो बाणैः प्रदिशश्च महारथः। पूरयामास तं दृष्ट्वा रामोऽपि सुमहद् धनुः॥ स सायकैर्दुर्विषहैर्विस्फुलिङ्गैरिवाग्निभिः। नभश्चकाराविवरं पर्जन्य इव वृष्टिभिः॥
en: And that mighty car-warrior covered all sides with his shafts. And secing this, Rāma of a tremendous bow with shafts incapable of being borne, and resembling tongues of flaming fire, entirely enveloped the welkin, even as a cloud pour down showers.

sa: वज्रस्य च निपातेन विरुजं त्वां समीक्ष्य च। सहस्रनेत्रः प्रीतात्मा ददौ ते वरमुत्तमम्॥ स्वच्छन्दतश्च मरणं तव स्यादिति वै प्रभो।
en: And seeing him sustain (serious) injury consequent on the impact of the thunder. He of a thousand eyes, pleased in his soul, also confer on (you) and excellent boon, O lord, saying, 'Your death: take place according to your will.' *Hanuman.

sa: शून्यान् दृष्ट्वा रथोपस्थान् मन्ये शोचन्ति पुत्रकाः। हिमात्यये यथा कक्षं शुष्कं दातेरितो महान्॥ अग्निहेत् तथा सेनां मामिकां स धनंजयः। आचक्ष्व मम तत् सर्वे कुशलो ह्यसि संजयः॥
en: And seeing also the terraces of their cars empty. Surely Dhananjaya is consuming my stoops like fire assisted by the wind, burning down a heap of straw dried by the heat of the sun that rises at the expiration of the winter season. O Sanjaya, expert as you are in storytelling, relate to me everything that happened.

sa: देही नित्यमवध्योऽयं देहे सर्वस्य भारत। तस्मात् सर्वाणि भूतानि न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि॥
en: This indestructible embodied self, O Bharata, is in the bodies of every one; therefore, you ought not to grieve for (the death of) all beings.

sa: ते तस्य कवचं भित्त्वा पपुः शोणितमाहवे। असूनिव विचिन्वन्तो देहे तस्य महात्मनः॥
en: Those arrows penetrating through Yudhisthira's armour drank, in that battle, his life-blood, as if plucking out all vitality invigorating the frame of that high-souled warrior.

sa: दृष्ट्वा पुत्रं च तं ग्रस्तं राहुणेव निशाकरम्। अभ्यद्रवत शैनेयं भारद्वाजः प्रतापवान्॥
en: Then beholding his son in that plight, like the moon devoured by Rahu, the highly powerful son of Bharadvaja rushed against the grandson of Shini.

sa: ततो रामो हृषितो राजसिंह दृष्ट्वा तदस्त्रं विनिवर्तितं वै।। रित्येव वाक्यं सहसा व्यमुञ्चत्॥ ततोऽपश्यत् पितरं जामदग्न्यः पितुस्तथा पितरं चास्य मान्यम्। रूचुश्चैनं सान्त्वपूर्व तदानीम्॥
en: Thereupon Rama, beholding that the Prasvapa weapon was withdrawn, was greatly excited and suddenly gave out these words, Fool that I am, I am vanquished, O Bhishma. Then the son of Jamadagni saw his father, and the venerable father of his father, who stood there surrounding him, and consoling him,

sa: एवं विभज्य योधास्तान् पृथक् च सह चैव ह। ज्वालावर्णो महेष्वासो द्रोणमंशमकल्पयत्॥
en: Having thus allotted among those warriors separately and collectively their respective tasks, that warrior, of the hue of fire, kept Drona for his own share,

sa: तेषां क्रोधं चिन्तयंस्तु अहःसु च निशासु च। न शान्तिमधिगच्छामि दुर्योधनकृतेन हि। कथं चाभून्महायुद्धं सवेमाचक्ष्व संजय॥
en: O Sanjaya, thinking of their anger, I never, by day or by night, enjoy any peace of mind on account of Duryodhana. How did the great battle take place? Tell me all about it.

sa: अब्रवीद् वेषमानश्च कन्यामाः सुदुःखितः। मा गाः पितुर्गृहं भद्रे मातुस्ते जनको ह्यहम्॥
en: Trembling, he said to that distressed and sorrowful girl: "Do not go to your father's place, gentle lady. I am the father of your mother.

sa: तथैव शकुनिः शूरः स्यालस्तव विशाम्पते। आरोपयद् स्थं तूर्णं गौतमं रथिनां वरम्॥
en: So also, O ruler of men, your heroic brother-in-law Shakuni, quickly took up on his chariot that foremost of car-warriors namely the son of Gautami.

sa: रथे रथे शतं चाश्वा बलिनो हेममालिनः। अश्वे अश्वे गोसहस्रं गवां पञ्चाशदाविकाः॥
en: With each car were a hundred horses adorned with chains of gold and with each horse a thousand cows. With each cow were fifty goats.

sa: वेगवद्भिर्हयैस्तैस्तु क्षोभिता पाण्डवी चमूः। निपतद्भिर्महावेगैर्हसैरिव महत् सरः॥ (तुरगैर्वायुवेगैश्च तत् सैन्यं व्याकुलीकृतम्।)
en: Then the army of the Pandavas was agitated by the charge of that fleetest horse division, like flight of swans suddenly alighting on its waters.

sa: देवव्रतत्वं विज्ञाप्य पृथिवीं सर्वराजसु! नैव हन्यां स्त्रियं जातु न स्त्रीपूर्वं कदाचन॥
en: Having proclaimed my religious vows among all the kings in the earth, “I shall never slay a woman or one that has been a woman.”

sa: न विशेषं विजानन्ति पुरस्य शिविरस्य वा। कुशला अपि राजेन्द्र नरा नगरवासिनः॥
en: And, O great king, even the clever men who lived in the city could not detect any distinguishing feature if their encampment from the city.

sa: यदि शक्यो मया जेतुं जामदग्न्यः प्रतापवान्। दैवतानि प्रसन्नानि दर्शयन्तु निशां मम॥
en: I indeed, it lies in my power to vanquish this powerful son of Jamadagni, let the gods, well-pleased, show themselves to me during the night.

sa: यथा वारयते वेला क्षुब्धतोयं महार्णवम्॥ तथैव पाण्डवं क्रुद्धं तव पुत्रो न्यवारयत्।
en: Just as the banks resist the mighty main with its waters agitated, so did your son resist that son of Pandu inflamed with rage. life,

sa: तस्मिन् द्रोणो बाणशतं पुत्रगृद्धी न्यपातयत्। अश्वत्थामा तथाष्टौ च परीप्सन पितरं रणे॥
en: Thereupon Drona desirous of saving his son, struck hundred shafts on Abhimanyu; and Ashvatthaman also desirous of rescuing his father, pierced him with sixty shafts.

sa: अशक्यं तु तमन्येन द्रोणं मत्वा युधिष्ठिरः। अविषहां गुरुं भारं सौभद्रं समवासृजत्॥
en: At last regarding Drona to be incapable of being checked by any one else, Yudhishthira placed that unbearable heavy burden on the son of Subhadra.

sa: तस्यां त्रस्ता नृपतयः सैनिकाश्च पृथग्विधाः। पाताल इव मज्जन्तो हीना देवव्रतेन ते॥
en: Then, in that army, bereft of Devavrata, the kings and the (common) soldiers, individually struck with panic, seemed to be sinking into the nethermost regions.

sa: निजघ्ने दशसाहस्रान् रामः परशुना तदा। न ह्यमृष्यत ता वाचो यास्तै शमुदीरिताः॥ भृगो रामाभिधावेति यदाक्रन्दन् द्विजोत्तमाः।
en: Then Rama slew with his axe ten thousand Kshatriyas. He then could not bear the hot words uttered by his enraged adversaries. When the twice-born sects exclaimed saying, 'O Rama, descendant of Bhrigu's race.

sa: अम्बायास्तां कथां श्रुत्वा काशिराज्ञश्च भारत। राजर्षिः स महातेजा बभूवोद्विग्नमानसः॥ पिता तदा।
en: Hearing those words of Amba, the daughter of the king of the Kashis, O Bharata, that royal sage of great energy became filled with pity.

sa: ततोऽहं ताश्च कन्या वै भ्रातुरर्थाय भारत। तच्च कर्म महाबाहो सत्यवत्यै न्यवेदयम्॥
en: Then did I make over, O Bharata, those girls to my brother, and submitted that deed, O you of long arms, to Satyavati for information.

sa: अथात्वरद् बलानि राजन् समरे निहत्य। त्रिगर्तराजो निहतान् समीक्ष्य महात्मना तानथ बन्धुवर्गान्॥
en: Ever-attended with victory, hide to slay Bhishma, having slain that division of kings. The king of the Trigaretas beholding those mighty car-warriors, his friends slain,

sa: मां हि पार्थ व्यपाश्रित्य येऽपि स्युः पापयोनयः। स्तेऽपि यान्ति परां गतिम्॥
en: Even those persons, Partha, who are of sinful birth, who are women, Vaishyas or Shudras, attain to the supreme goal, if they come to Me..

sa: अविषह्यतमा ह्येते निश्चिताः पार्थ षड्रथाः। एतानजित्वा षड् रथान् नैव प्राप्यो जयद्रथः॥
en: These six warriors, O Partha, are surely exceedingly difficult of being borne down, Without first vanquishing these six carwarriors, you cannot hope to reach Jayadratha.

sa: युधिष्ठिर उवाच पृच्छामि त्वा द्विजश्रेष्ठ शृणु यन्मेऽभिकाक्षितम्। कथं जयेयं संग्रामे भवन्तमपराजितम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said O foremost of Brahmanas, I ask you, hear what I have to say. How shall we in battle defeat you who are invincible?

sa: दृष्ट्वा मां तूर्णमायान्तं दंशितं स्यन्दने स्थितम्। अकरोद् रथमत्यर्थं रामः सज्ज प्रतापवान्॥
en: Seeing me coming quickly with my coat of mail on and seated on my chariot Rama, of great luster, got ready his car very carefully.

sa: दृष्ट्वा विषक्तं कौन्तेयं कृतवर्मरथं प्रति। चिन्तयामास वार्ष्णेयो न नः कालात्ययो भवेत्॥
en: Beholding the son of Kunti engaged with the mighty-warrior Kritavarman, the descendant of the Vrishni race (Krishna) thought that there was no time to waste.

sa: तत्रासुरवधं कृत्वा सर्वलोकसुखाय वै। धर्मं प्राप्य यशः प्राप्य योगं प्राप्स्यसि तत्त्वतः॥
en: There, for the well being of the world slaughtering the Asuras, and establishing righteousness and winning glory, you shall again attain to the best Yoga.

sa: भीष्ममेव प्रपद्यस्व न तेऽन्या विद्यते गतिः। निर्जितो ह्यस्मि भीष्मेण महास्त्राणि प्रमुञ्चता॥
en: Take refuge even with Bhishma himself; there exists no other for you. I am vanquished by Bhishma on account of his using such mighty weapons.

sa: तमागम्य तु राजानं दशार्णाधिपतिं तदा। तद् वाक्यमाददे राजन् यदुक्तं द्रुपदेन ह॥
en: Approaching the king, viz., the lord of the Dasharna land he gave the reply, O king, as it had been spoken, O king, by Drupada.

sa: ततः शब्दो महानासीत् पुत्राणां तव भारत। रथघोषश्च विपुलो वादित्राणां च निस्वनः॥
en: Then, O Bharata, loud were the war cries uttered by your sons, and defending was clatter of chariots and the sound of the musical instruments.

sa: तत् प्रभग्नं बलं दृष्ट्वा पिता देवव्रतस्तव। अब्रवीत् समरे शूरं भारद्वाजं स्मयन्निव॥
en: Your sire Devavrata then, on seeing the Kuru army routed, smilingly thus spoke to the heroic son of Bharadvaja (Drona) on that field of battle.

sa: द्रोणानीकं दुरासदम्। तत् कर्माद्य करिष्यामि हितं यद् वंशयोर्द्वयोः। मातुलस्य च यत् प्रीतिं करिष्यति पितुश्च मे॥
en: I will this day achieve that feat that will redound to the good of both the families (of my father and mother). I will do what will please my sire and my maternal uncle.

sa: सदृशं कर्मणस्तस्य फलं प्राप्नुहि भारत। करोमि कामं कं तेऽद्य प्रवृणीष्व यमिच्छसि॥
en: O Bharata, reap the adequate fruit of that act of yours. What desire of yours shall I fulfill now? Ask whatever boon you may like?"

sa: संजय उवाच ततो मुहूर्तात् तुमुलः शब्दो हृदयकम्पनः। अश्रूयत महाराज योधानां प्रयुयुत्सताम्॥
en: Sanjaya said O king, a loud uproar was soon after heard. It was made by the combatants ready to fight. It made all hearts tremble.

sa: अन्तमद्य गमिष्यामि यदि नोत्सृजसे रणम्। एवमुक्त्वा तु हैडिम्बो महद् विस्फार्य कार्मुकम्॥
en: Will I this avenge, if indeed you do not fly forsaking the field of battle.' Having thus spoken, and stretching his mighty bow Hidimba's son,

sa: तस्मात् पार्थं पुरोधाय पञ्चालान् संजयांस्तथा। मद्वधे क्रियतां यत्नो मम चेदिच्छसि प्रियम्॥
en: So if you desire to do me a good turn, strive your best for slaying me, placing the Panchalas and Srinjayas with Partha, before yourself."

sa: हत्वा सुयोधन त्वां वै सहितं सर्वसोदरैः। आक्रमिष्ये पदा मूर्ध्नि धर्मराजस्य पश्यतः॥
en: Slaying yourself, O Suyodhana, with all your brothers, I shall strike you on the head with my feet in the sight of the virtuous king.”

sa: यत्र शेते नरश्रेष्ठः शरतल्पे पितामहः॥ ते तु भीष्मं समासाद्य ऋषयो हंसरूपिणः।
en: At the spot where that foremost of men was lying on his arrowy bed. Then coming to Bhishma those sages under the forms of swans,

sa: मम तु व्यसनस्यास्य भीष्मो मूलं महाव्रतः। येनाहं वशमानीता समुक्षिप्य बलात् तदा॥
en: The root of this distress of mine is Bhishma of great vows, since by him was I brought under subjection taking me up by force.

sa: सैनिकाच मुदा युक्ता वर्धयन्ति द्विजोत्तमम्। दुर्योधनं पुरस्कृत्य प्रार्थयन्तो महद् यशः। दुर्योधनं ततो राजन् द्रोणो वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Then the soldiers also filled with delight and desirous of earning fame, began to extol that foremost of regenerate ones, with Duryodhana at their head. Thereupon, O monarch, Drona spoke these words of Duryodhana.

sa: नैते जातु पुनयुद्धमीहेयुरिति मे मतिः। यथा तु भग्ना द्रोणेन वातेनेव महाद्रुमाः॥
en: Meseems they will never again seek to fight, in as much as they are now broken by Drona like mighty trees broken by the tempest.

sa: सा तत्र परमं तीव्र चचार व्रतमुत्तमम्। सा तदा ह्येकपादेन तस्थौ पद्मानि षोडश॥ पञ्च चाब्दानि कारुण्यात् प्रजानां तु हितैषिणी। इन्द्रियाणीनिद्रयार्थेभ्यः प्रियेभ्यः संनिवर्त्य सा॥
en: There she practised a vow excellent and greatly severe. There she stood on one leg for sixteen times ten billions of years and five times ten billions also, through compassion for living creatures and through desire for doing them good, all the time withholding her senses from their dear objects.

sa: तस्य कालेन महता विश्रम्भं जग्मुरण्डजाः। समेत्य च प्रशंसन्ति मार्जारं तं विशाम्पते॥
en: In course of time birds had much confidence in him and having assembled together they began to praise the cat, O lord of the universe..

sa: एष व्यूहामि ते व्यूहं राजसत्तम दुर्जयम्। अचलं नाम वज्राख्यं विहितं वज्रपाणिना॥
en: O foremost of kings, that immovable Vyuha called Vajra which was designed by the wielder of thunderbolt (Indra), that impenetrable Vyuha I shall make today.

sa: अथ चित्तं समाधातुं न शक्नोषि मयि स्थिरम्। अभ्यासयोगेन ततो मामिच्छाप्तुं धनंजय॥
en: If, however, O Dhananjaya, you are unable thus to fix your mind on Me, then, try to obtain Me by devotion arising from continued application.

sa: पश्य वीर यथा ह्येष फाल्गुनस्य सुतो बली। मायावी विप्रियं कर्तुमकार्षीन्मे बलक्षयम्॥
en: 'Behold O hero, how this puissant son of Arjuna, versed in illusions, has done me this terrible wrong in the shape of destroying my forces?

sa: यत्र काले त्वनावृत्तिमावृतिं चैव योगिनः। प्रयाता यान्ति तं कालं वक्ष्यामि भरतर्षभ॥
en: I will state the times, O best of the Bharata race, at which Yogis, departing from this world, go never to return, or, to return.

sa: तं दृष्ट्वा क्षत्रियाः शूराः प्रतपन्तं तरस्विनम्। द्विफाल्गुनमिमं लोकं मेनिरे तस्य कर्मभिः॥
en: Beholding him fall upon them with celerity, the heroic Kshatriyas considered, in consequence of the feats accomplished by him, that the world contained two Phalguna.

sa: रूपं चाप्रतिमं तस्य त्रिदशेश्चापि दुर्लभम्॥ अपश्यतो हि वीरस्य का शान्तिर्हृदयस्य मे।
en: His beauty that was unequaled and scarce even among the heaven-dwelling gods. Oh, without beholding that beauty of his, what peace can my heart enjoy?

sa: बृहत्क्षत्रं तु कैकेयं कृपः शारद्वतो ययौ। तं कृपः शरवर्षेण च्छादयामास भारत॥
en: The son of Sharadvata, Kripa, attacked the ruler of the Kaikeyas named Brihatkshatra. O descendant of Bharata, Kripa covered him with a shower of arrows.

sa: संनिवार्य शरांन्तांस्तु कृपः शारद्वतो युधि। चेकितानं रणे यत्तं राजन् विव्याध पत्रिभिः॥
en: Resisting also those arrows, in that combat, Kripa the son of Sharadvata pierced 0 monarch, with winged shafts, Chekitana who had been fighting very heedfully.

sa: शाकद्वीपं च वक्ष्यामि यथावदिह पार्थिव। शृणु मे त्वं यथान्यायं ब्रुवतः कुरुनन्दन॥
en: O descendant of Bharata. O scion of the Kuru race, I shall now speak to you in detail of Shakadvipa. Hear as I describe it.

sa: भीमं ते विव्यधुस्तूर्णं शल्यहेतोररिंदमाः॥ स च तान् प्रतिविव्याध पञ्चभिः पञ्चभिः शरैः।
en: All these subduers of foes, then quickly pierced Bhima (with arrows), for rescuing Shalya. He (Bhima) also pierced them in return, each with five shafts,

sa: पत्र पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति। तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः॥
en: I accept leaf, flowers, fruits, water, from him who is pure, and who with faith offers them to Me, if they are presented with devotion.

sa: इच्छेयं त्वत्प्रसादाद्धि तपस्तप्तुं प्रजेश्वर। प्रदिशेमं वरं देव त्वं मह्यं भगवन् प्रभो॥
en: O Lord of the creation, I desire to carry on ascetic austerities through your grace. O great Lord, O divine being, accord me this boon.

sa: द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके क्षरश्चाक्षर एव च। क्षरः सर्वाणि भूतानि कूटस्थोऽक्षर उच्यते॥
en: There are two entities in this universe, namely the Perishable and the Imperishable. All creatures are the Perishable, and the unconcerned One is the Imperishable.

sa: न ते युद्धान्निवर्तन्ते धर्मोपेता महाबलाः। श्रिया परमया युक्ता यतो धर्मस्ततो जयः॥
en: Attended by excellent prosperity and endued with great strength and conforming to all morality, they never turn back from the fight. Victory ever attends righteousness.

sa: मत्वा तृणेन तांस्तुल्यान् विचचार गतव्यथः॥ ते चापि रथिनां श्रेष्ठा भीमाय निशिताञ्छरान्। प्रेषयामासुरव्यग्राः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥ तस्य शक्तिं महावेगां भगदत्तो महारथः। चिक्षेप समरे वीरः स्वर्णदण्डां महामते॥ तोमरं सैन्धवो राजा पट्टिशं च महाभुजः।
en: Yet regarding them as mere straws, he careered through the field without the least pain. Those foremost of car-warriors also patiently sped at Bhima sharp arrows by hundreds and thousands. Then the highly powerful heroic Bhagadatta let go his lance of great velocity and of a golden staff at that illustrious warrior Bhima. The mighty-armed king of the Sindhus hurled at the latter a lance and a battle-axe.

sa: प्रविभागो न राष्ट्राणां पुराणां चाभवत् तदा। यथासुखं यथाकामं तथैता मुदिताः प्रजाः॥
en: His dominions and his cities were not divided into smaller sections and countries. There his subjects lived delightedly, as it suited their desire or convenience.

sa: भीष्मः कथं महात्मा सन् संस्थाता दक्षिणायने॥ इत्युक्त्वा प्रस्थिता हंसा दक्षिणामभितो दिशम्।
en: “Why should the high-souled Bhishma pass away when the sun is in the Southern solstice." Having thus spoken, the swans flew towards the Southern directions.

sa: ततः सर्वान् नरव्याघ्रो हत्वा नरपतीन् रणे। कौरवांश्च महाबाहुः कुन्त्यैदद्यात् स मेदिनीम्॥
en: Then that foremost of men, that mightyarmed hero, having slain in battle the Kauravas and the (assembled) monarchs will offer the whole earth of Kunti.

sa: अन्तवत्तु फलं तेषां वेदाहं समतीतानि वर्तमानानि चार्जुन। भविष्याणि च भूतानि मां तु वेद न कश्चन॥
en: O Arjuna, I know the things that are past; I know all things that are present and (know also) all things that will be in the future. But there is none who knows Me.

sa: ततो द्युतिमतां मध्ये पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम्। सृञ्जयानां च मत्स्यानां कृष्णस्य च यशस्विनः॥
en: Then in the midst of those men of effulgence, those great-souled son of Pandu and the Srinjayas and the Matsya's and also the renowned Krishna,

sa: सुयोधनो मम वचो वक्तव्यो नृपतेः सुतः। अहं द्रोणं हनिष्यामि सगणं सहबान्धवम्॥
en: Suyodhana, the son of the king should thus be spoken to, on my behalf. “I shall kill Drona along with his host and his friends.

sa: ततः सुयोधनो दृष्ट्वा हतमाधिरथिं त्वया। निराशो जीविते त्वद्य राज्ये चैव भवत्वरिः॥
en: And then let the enemy Suyodhana, witness in today Adhiratha's son thus fall a victim to your arms, despair of his life and his sovereignty.

sa: पुच्छे ह्यास्तां महावीर्यो भ्रातरौ पार्थिवौ तदा। चित्रश्च चित्रसेनश्च महत्या सेनया वृतौ॥
en: Thereupon the two royal brothers, Chitra and Chitrasena, of iminense prowess having been accompanied by a vast army, stood in the tail (of the Makara).

sa: एवमुक्ते तु काकेन प्रहस्यैको विहंगमः॥ उवाच काकं राधेय वचनं तन्निबोध मे।
en: Having been thus addressed by the crow, O son of Radha, one of the swans said to him laughing. Hear from me (what he said).

sa: प्रविश्य च महत् सैन्यं शल्य: परबलार्दनः। न्ययच्छत् तुरगान् हृष्टो यत्र यत्रैच्छरग्रणीः॥
en: On penetrating into that vast array, Shalya, the avenger of foes, took Karna to the very spot that foremost of warriors wished to be in.

sa: आजगाम पुनर्दीपं स्पर्धया पेततुर्यतः। संस्थाप्य तं चापि पुनः समाश्वास्य च खेचरम्॥
en: Having placed speedily the crow who was besides himself on his back he came to the island from which they had started challenging each other.

sa: अद्य दुर्योधन राजा आत्मानं चानुशोचताम्॥ हते कर्णे मया संख्ये सपुत्रे ससुहजने।
en: Let king Duryodhana also indulge himself in grief, today, as Karna falls a victim to my arms in company with all his sons and relations.

sa: संजय उवाच अपराह्ने महाराज सूतपुत्रः प्रतापवान्। जघान सोमकान् सर्वान् भीमसेनस्य पश्यतः॥
en: Sanjaya said O king, the valiant son of Suta began to strike down the Somaka troops, in that afternoon, even on very face of Bhimasena.

sa: यदि तेऽस्ति युयुत्साद्य मया सह नराधिप। निर्दयो निशितैर्बाणैः प्रहर प्रहरामि ते॥
en: If, O lord of men, you are desirous of fighting with me, strike me with sharpened arrows and I also will strike you (in return).

sa: ततोऽस्य वाहान् समरे शर्निन्ये यमक्षयम्। सारथिं च रथात् तूर्णं पातयामास पत्रिणा॥
en: Thereafter that slayer of foes dispatched to the abode of Death the horses of Duryodhana and he also felled quickly the charioteer of the latter.

sa: दक्षिणे तु महाराज सुषेणः सत्यसंगरः। वृतो रथसहस्रेण दन्तिनां च त्रिभिः शतै॥
en: O great king, Sushena of certain resolution was stationed in the right hind-foot, encompassed by a force of one thousand cars and three hundred elephants.

sa: कृतवर्मा तु संक्रुद्धो धर्मपुत्रस्य मारिष। धनुश्चिच्छेद भल्लेन तं च विव्याध सप्तभिः॥
en: O worshipful sire, Kritavarma too, fired with rage, cut-off the bow of the Dharmaraja with a broad-headed dart and then pierced him with seven (arrows).

sa: स तानि शरजालानि गदाः प्रासांश्च वीर्यवान्। आगतानग्रसत् पार्थः सरितः सागरो यथा॥
en: Then the highly puissant son of Pritha received those showers of arrows, lances and maces, like the ocean receiving the numerous rivers flowing into it.

sa: ततः प्रभातसमये राजन् कर्णस्य दैवतैः। अन्येषां चैव योधानां सा बुद्धिर्नाश्यते पुनः॥
en: When however, the day dawned, 0 monarch, as fate would have it, Karna as well as all the other warriors forget all about that resolution.

sa: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच अहन्यहनि मे दीप्तं यशः पतति संजय। हता मे बहवो योधा मन्ये कालस्य पर्ययम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Day by day, O Sanjaya, by blazing fame is dwindling away. Numerous warriors of my side are being slain. I consider all this to be due to the adverse influence of Fate.

sa: प्रपेततुः स्पर्धया च ततस्तौ हंसवायसौ॥ एकपाती च चक्राङ्गः काकः पातशतेन च। पेतिवानथ चक्राङ्ग पेतिवानथ वायसः॥
en: Then those two, the swan the crow, rose into the sky challenging each other-the swan coursing in one motion and the crow in a hundred different ways. The swan flew and the crow flew.

sa: अद्य मे विक्रम पार्थो विज्ञास्यति धनंजयः। त्वयि भूमौ विनिहते शयाने रुधिरोक्षिते॥
en: Today Pritha's son Dhananjaya will come to know of my prowess when he will see you slain by me and lie weltering in your blood.

sa: यानर्जुनः सभृकुटीकटाक्षं कर्णाय राजन्नसृजन्जितारिः। तान् सायकैर्यसते सूतपुत्रः क्षिप्तान् क्षिप्तान् पाण्डवस्याशु संघान्॥
en: But O King, all those arrows and the successive ones, shot by Arjuna, that contracted brow, were all destroyed by Karna by his own shafts.

sa: तत्र नो ग्लहमानानां ध्रुवौ जयपराजयौ॥ यत्र ते परमेष्वासा यत्ता रक्षन्ति सैन्धवम्।
en: O sire, there indeed will our victory of defeat be known where those fierce bowmen are exerting themselves in protecting the king of the Sindhus.

sa: सेनापतिर्भविष्यामि तवाहं नात्र संशयः। स्थिरो भव महाराज जितान् विद्धि च पाण्डवान्॥४१
en: I will be your generalissimo, there is not doubt about it. O powerful monarch, have peace. And do you think the Pandavas were already conquered.

sa: तं दृष्ट्वा विस्थं तत्र भ्रातरोऽस्य महारथाः। अन्ववर्तन्त वेगेन महत्या सेनया सह॥
en: Witnessing that (sad) plight that their brother was in, his brothers, who were great car-warriors, followed by a large army, rushed furiously to that place.

sa: सैन्धवं दशभिर्गाणैर्वृषसेनं त्रिभिः शरैः। शारद्वतं च विंशत्या विद्ध्वा पार्थो ननाद ह॥
en: He pierced the Sindhu ruler with Vallas and Vrishasena with three arrows and then piercing the son of Saradvata, Pritha's son uttered a loud war-cry.

sa: विररामरणात् तस्मात् पश्यतां सर्वधन्विनाम्। एवं तं विरथं कृत्वा कर्णो राजन् व्यकत्थयत्॥
en: Refrained from that fight before they very eyes of the bowmen present. Thus o king, making Bhima carless, Karna reproved him in such harsh language.

sa: अत्यन्तसुखसंवृद्धो मानितश्च महारथः। कृती च सततं पार्थ नित्यं द्वेष्टि च बान्धवान्॥
en: Reared in all luxury, he is highly esteemed by all the mighty car-warriors. O Partha, he is accomplished and the constant hater of the Pandavas.

sa: दन्तवेष्टेषु नेत्रेषु कुम्भेषु च कटेषु च। मर्मस्वपि च मर्मज्ञस्तान नागानवधीद् बली॥
en: The powerful hero, conversant with vital parts, killed all those elephants striking them on their temples, frontal globes eyes and in parts above the gums.

sa: अविद्धं तत्र नाद्राक्षं युयुधानस्य सायकः। न तादृक् कदनं राजन् कृतवांस्तत्र फाल्गुनः॥
en: We then beheld none who was not pierced will the arrows of Yuyudhana. Even Phaiguna himselt () king, spread not such carnage in your rooms.

sa: संजय उवाच ततः शल्यः परिष्वज्य सुतं ते वाक्यमब्रवीत्। दुर्योधनममित्रघ्न प्रीतो मद्रधिपस्तदा॥
en: Sanjaya said Thereupon Shalya, that king of the Madras, being highly gratified, after having embraced your son, Duryodhana, that slayer of enemies, addressed him, saying.

sa: तावद्भिरथ तान् भीमो व्योम्नि चिच्छेद पत्रिभिः। नाराचान् सूतपुत्रस्य तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: With as many winged shafts, Bhima then cut-off those Narachas sped by Suta's sons when they were coursing through the sky and said wait, wait.

sa: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच यत्तत् प्रविश्य पार्थानां सैन्यं कुर्वञ्जनक्षयम्। कर्णो राजानमभ्येत्य तन्माचक्ष्व संजय॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Tell me, O Sanjaya, how Karna, having caused a great carnage and entered into the midst of the Pandavas assailed the king Yudhishthira.

sa: नाहं भीषयितुं शक्यो वामात्रेण कथंचन। अन्यं जानिहि यः शक्यस्त्वया भीषयितुं रणे।॥
en: I am not to be frightened by mere words. O Shalya, he, whom you will be able to frighten in battle, is some other person.

sa: न हि कर्णः समुद्भूतो भयार्थमिह मद्रका विक्रमार्थमहं जातो यशोऽर्थं च तथाऽऽत्मनः॥
en: Karna is not born for fear in battle, O Madraka. I am rather born to display my valour and achieve glory for my own self.

sa: त्वदृते पुरुषव्याघ्र य एतद् योधयेद् बलम्। महाप्रभावा बहवस्त्वया तुल्याधिकाऽपि वा॥ समेताः पृथिव गला धार्तराष्ट्रस्य कारणात्। ते त्वां प्राप्य रणे क्रुद्धा नाभ्यवर्तन्त दंशिताः॥
en: Capable of encountering these forces, besides you, O most valiant of men. Numerous lords of the earth, endowed with great prowess and either equal or superior to you, have, at the command of Dhritarashtra assembled together. (But) those (warriors). clad in armour, could not withstand your wrathful self in battle.

sa: स्थिरा बुद्धिनरेन्द्रस्य धार्तराष्ट्रस्य मानद॥ कर्णः पार्थान् रणे सर्वान् विजेष्यति न संशयः।
en: O giver of honours, it is the firm belief of the royal Dhartarashtras that Karna will, to a certainty, slay all the Parthas in battle.

sa: कर्ण पश्य महारङ्गे ज्वलन्तमिव पावकम्। असौ भीमो महेष्वासः सनिवृत्तो रणं प्रति॥
en: Look, Karna is illuminating like a fire blazed on the great stage of the war and the great warrior Bhimasena has returned to the battle-field.

sa: तस्य शङ्खस्य नादेन धनुषो निःस्वनेन च। निःसत्त्वाश्च ससत्त्वाश्च क्षितौ पेतुस्तदा जनाः॥
en: In consequence of that twang of the Gandiva and the blast of that conch, all the Kuru-people, strong or weak, fell down on the Earth.

sa: देवासुरमनुष्येषु प्रख्यातौ यौ नरोत्तमौ। तौ मावमंस्था मौात् त्वं खद्योत इव रोचनौ॥८५
en: Those two best of men are well-known among the gods, Asuras and men; you are a fire-fly, do not foolishly disregard those two bright luminaries.

sa: अभिद्रवत गृह्णीत हयान् द्रोणस्य धावत। इति स्म चुक्रुशुः सर्वे राजपुत्राः सराजकाः॥
en: 'Rush,' 'seize the running steeds of Drona,' these were the words that were then uttered loudly by the kings and princes of the Kaurava host.

sa: ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजंस्तत्यक्त्वा द्रौणिं महाहवे। प्रवयौ तावकं सौन्यं युक्तः क्रूराय कर्मणे॥
en: Yudhishthira then, O king, thus avoiding the son of Drona in the great battle, marched against your army being determined to wage a ruthless slaughter.

sa: विन्दं तु निहतं दृष्ट्वा ह्यनुविन्दः प्रतापवान्। हताश्वं रथमुत्सृज्य गदां गृह्य महाबलः॥
en: The highly puissant Anuvinda, beholding Vinda thus slain, left the car of which the steeds were slain; and that mighty hero, taking up a mace.

sa: न भीमसेनं सम्प्राप्य निवर्तेत कदाचन। पतङ्गा इव वह्निं ते प्राविशन्नल्पचेतसः॥ ये भीमसेनं संक्रुद्धमन्वधावन् विमोहिताः। यत् तत् सभायां भीमेन मम पुत्रवधाश्रयम्॥ उक्तं संरम्भिणोग्रेण कुरूणां शृण्वतां तदा। तन्नूनमभिसंचिन्त्य दृष्ट्वा कर्ण च निर्जितम्॥
en: But it not possible for them to come back alive after an encounter with Bhima. Those who foolishly assail Bhimasena when he is inflamed with rage are-like insects rushing on the blazing flames of a fire. Such thinking what the irate Bhima of fearful hands had said to the assembly in the hearing of the Kurus about the slaughter of my sons and beholding the defeat of Karna.

sa: तं षभिः सायकैनॊणः साश्वयन्तारमार्दयेत्। स तं न ममृषे द्रोणं युयुधानो महारथः॥
en: Drona in return, with six arrows, afflicted him and his steeds and charioteer. Then that mighty car-warrior Yuyudhana could not brook that act of Drona.

sa: जहि कर्णं रणे शूरं सात्वतेन सहायवान्। यथेन्द्रस्तारकं पूर्वं स्कन्देन सह जनिवान्॥
en: Supported by the Satvata hero, do you slay the heroic Karna in battle, even as Indra supported by Skanda slew Taraka in days gone by.”

sa: श्रुतं ते गदतो वाक्यं सर्वमेतन्मयाच्युत। न्याययुक्तं च चित्रं च फाल्गुनार्थे यशस्करम्॥
en: “O you of unfading glory, I have heard all the words you have spoken for Arjuna's sake-words that are delightful, equitable and conducive to fame.

sa: ते दृष्ट्वा सहसा पार्थे गोप्तारः सैन्धवस्य तु। चक्रुर्नादान् महेष्वासाः कम्पयन्तो वसुंधराम्॥
en: Then suddenly seeing Partha before them, those guards of Jayadratha the Sindnu-king, all mighty bowmen, uttered a fierce shout, causing the earth to tremble therewith.

sa: तेन तस्य रथो भाति मयूरेण महात्मनः॥ यथा स्कन्दस्य राजेन्द्र मयूरेण विराजता।
en: With that peacock, the car of that illustrious hero appeared as beautiful as the car of Skanda, O king, appears, being decked by his peacock.

sa: अश्मवर्षं सुतुमलं विससर्ज घटोत्कचे॥ अश्मवर्षं स तं घोरं शरवर्षेण वीर्यवान्। दिक्षु विध्वंसयामास तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥ ततो नानाप्रहरणैरन्योन्यमभिवर्षताम्।
en: Began to pour a heavy downpour of stones on Ghatotkacha. That terrible shower of stones, the brave Ghatotkacha baffled by means of a shower of arrows. They then poured on each other diverse weapons.

sa: स भवान् मर्षयत्येतांस्त्वत्तो भीतान् विशेषतः। शिष्यत्वं वा पुरस्कृत्य मम वा मन्दभाग्यताम्॥
en: The Pandavas are all afraid of you. Yet you always forgive them remembering perhaps that they are your disciples or owing to my unfortunate luck."

sa: सर्वत्र सन्ति राजानः स्वं स्वं धर्ममनुव्रताः। दुर्मनुष्यान् निगृह्णन्ति सन्ति सर्वत्र धार्मिका॥
en: In every country there are kings observant of their own religions and engaged in repressing the wicked. And in every country there are virtuous men.

sa: नेमौ शक्यौ महेष्वासौ युद्धे क्षपयितुं परैः। इच्छमानौ पुनरिमौ हन्येतां सामरं जगत्॥
en: None of these two combatants could be resisted by the foe in battle. At their will they can destroy the universe with the gods themselves.

sa: भूयोऽहं त्वां विजयिनं परिष्वज्यामि पार्षत। सूतपुत्रे हते पापे धार्तराष्ट्रे च संयुगे॥
en: "O son of Prisata, I will again embrace your victorious self, when the sinful sons of Suta and Dhritarashtra will be slain in the battle.

sa: तथास्य सशरं चापं हस्तावापं च मारिष॥ क्षुरप्रेण सुतीक्ष्णेन राजा चिच्छेद संयुगे।
en: Then the king, O sire, cut-off, in the fight, with his razor-shaped arrow his enemy's bow and the leathern fence with the arrows fixed thereon.

sa: बाल्यवृत्तानि सर्वाणि प्रीयमाणौ विचिन्त्य तौ। अन्योन्यं प्रेक्षमाणौ च स्मयमानौ पुनः पुनः॥
en: Recollecting their conduct towards each other in their early days and reflecting with pleasure on the same, they looked at each other and smiled repeatedly.

sa: इदमिन्द्रेण ते साक्षादुपदिष्टं महात्मना। अस्त्रं रुद्रेण वा पार्थ द्रोणेनाथ कृपेण वा॥
en: Was it for this that you learnt the use of weapons from the illustrious Indra or Rudra or Drona or Kripa. O son of Pritha!

sa: देवास्तु पितृभिः सार्ध सगणा: सपदानुगाः। यमो वैश्रवणश्चैव वरुणश्च यतोऽर्जुनः॥ ब्रह्य क्षत्रं च यज्ञाश्च दक्षिणाश्चार्जुनं श्रिताः।
en: The Pitris and the heavenly bodies with all their followers and staff, Yama and Vaicravam and Varuna were for Arjuna. The Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, the gifts (Dakshinas), the sacred sacrifices were in favor of Arjuna.

sa: देवब्रह्मनृपर्षीणां गणाः पाण्डवतोऽभवन्॥ तुम्बुरुप्रमुखा राजन् गन्धर्वाश्च यतोऽर्जुनः। प्राधेया सहमौनेया गन्धर्वाप्सरसां गणाः॥
en: The different sets of Rajarshis were for the son of Pandu. O monarch, all the Gandharvas with Tumburu as their head were in Arjuna's favor.

sa: अद्य तेऽपचितिं कृत्वा शितैमाधव सायकैः। तस्त्रियो नन्दयिष्यामि ये त्वया निहता रणे॥
en: O Madhava, today, slaying you with my sharp arrows, I shall afford delight to the wives of those who have been slain by you. in

sa: प्रतिलभ्य ततः संज्ञा चित्रसेनो महारथः। धनुश्चिच्छेद भल्लेन तं च विव्याध सप्तभिः॥
en: Thereupon Chitrasena, that mighty bowman, having attained consciousness again, struck down his enemy's bow by a broodheaded shafts and also pierced him with seven arrows.
